notes: Short declarative lines often land a scene after one longer setup.

recurringWords.note: Used for both streets and personal choices.

recurringPhrases.note: Returns as a practical refrain after a mistake.

terms.usage: Appears only in frustrated dialogue, never as decoration.

profanityRegister.note: The synthetic source uses mild profanity sparingly and in character.

humorMechanics.name: practical-understatement
humorMechanics.description: A character answers a large problem with an overly practical observation.

openings.name: object-in-motion
openings.description: A concrete object begins moving before its history is explained.

turns.name: errand-reframed
turns.description: A failed task reveals a different promise worth keeping.

landings.name: quiet-object-return
landings.description: The scene closes on the ordinary object carrying new meaning.

firstPersonHabits: The narrator admits what was misunderstood before explaining anyone else's motive.

tenseUsage.note: Past tense carries the scene and its action.
Present tense appears in brief reflective conclusions.

negativeSpace: Never turns an uncertain memory into a universal lesson.
Never stacks rhetorical questions to manufacture suspense.

preserve: Keep the concrete object and the final understated turn.
adapt: Break the route into one visible decision per slide.
avoid: Do not turn the final line into a motivational slogan.

preserve: Keep the narrator's early admission of error.
adapt: Let each post advance the errand rather than summarize it.
avoid: Do not add a numbered life-lesson list.
